CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,
    cardKingdomId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Id, Column Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator,
    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,
    duelDeck TEXT -- Column Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.,
    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,
    faceConvertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face,
    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to find the Italian text ruling for cards in the 'Coldsnap' set. This requires joining the 'foreign_data' table (for Italian text) with the 'cards' table (to identify the cards) and the 'set_translations' table (to identify the set 'Coldsnap'). The set code is needed to join sets and cards. The language and text columns are needed from foreign_data to filter by Italian and retrieve the text, respectively. The name column is needed from cards to identify the card. The set_translations table is needed to filter by the set name.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T3.text
FROM set_translations AS T1
INNER JOIN cards AS T2
  ON T1.setCode = T2.setCode
INNER JOIN foreign_data AS T3
  ON T2.uuid = T3.uuid
WHERE T1.translation = 'Coldsnap' AND T3.language = 'Italian';

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to find the Italian text ruling for cards in the 'Coldsnap' set. This requires joining the 'foreign_data' table (for Italian text) with the 'cards' table (to identify the cards) and the 'set_translations' table (to identify the set 'Coldsnap'). The set code is needed to join sets and cards. The language and text columns are needed from foreign_data to filter by Italian and retrieve the text, respectively. The name column is needed from cards to identify the card. The set_translations table is needed to filter by the set name.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.text FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN set_translations AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.setCode WHERE T3.translation = 'Coldsnap' AND T1.language = 'Italian'

CREATE TABLE cards (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL,
    artist TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the artist that illustrated the card art.,
    asciiName TEXT -- Column Description: The ASCII(opens new window) (Basic/128) code formatted card name with no special unicode characters.,
    availability TEXT -- Column Description: A list of the card's available printing types., Column Value Explanation: "arena", "dreamcast", "mtgo", "paper", "shandalar",
    borderColor TEXT -- Column Description: The color of the card border., Column Value Explanation: "black", "borderless", "gold", "silver", "white",
    cardKingdomFoilId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Foil Id, Column Value Explanation: cardKingdomFoilId, when paired with cardKingdomId that is not Null, is incredibly powerful.,
    cardKingdomId TEXT -- Column Description: card Kingdom Id, Column Value Explanation: A list of all the colors in the color indicator,
    colorIdentity TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors found in manaCost, colorIndicator, and text,
    colorIndicator TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in the color indicator (The symbol prefixed to a card's types).,
    colors TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all the colors in manaCost and colorIndicator., Column Value Explanation: Some cards may not have values, such as cards with "Devoid" in its text.,
    convertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost of the card. Use the manaValue property., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana,
    duelDeck TEXT -- Column Description: The indicator for which duel deck the card is in.,
    edhrecRank INTEGER -- Column Description: The card rank on EDHRec,
    faceConvertedManaCost REAL -- Column Description: The converted mana cost or mana value for the face for either half or part of the card., Column Value Explanation: if value is higher, it means that this card cost more converted mana for the face,
    faceName TEXT -- Column Description: The name on the face of the card.,
    flavorName TEXT -- Column Description: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The promotional card name printed above the true card name on special cards that has no game function.,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function., Column Value Explanation: The italicized text found below the rules text that has no game function.,
    frameEffects TEXT -- Column Description: The visual frame effects., Column Value Explanation: "colorshifted", "companion", "compasslanddfc", "devoid", "draft", "etched", "extendedart", "fullart", "inverted", "legendary", "lesson", "miracle", "mooneldrazidfc", "nyxtouched", "originpwdfc", "showcase", "snow", "sunmoondfc", "textless", "tombstone", "waxingandwaningmoondfc",
    frameVersion TEXT -- Column Description: The version of the card frame style., Column Value Explanation: "1993", "1997", "2003", "2015", "future",
    hand TEXT -- Column Description: The starting maximum hand size total modifier., Column Value Explanation: A + or - character precedes an integer.   positive maximum hand size: +1, +2, .... negative maximum hand size: -1, .... neural maximum hand size: 0....,
    hasAlternativeDeckLimit INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card allows a value other than 4 copies in a deck., Column Value Explanation: 0: disallow 1: allow,
    hasContentWarning INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card marked by Wizards of the Coast (opens new window) for having sensitive content. See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,
    hasFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    hasNonFoil INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card can be found in non-foil, Column Value Explanation: 0: cannot be found 1: can be found,
    isAlternative INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is an alternate variation to an original printing, Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is only available in online game variations., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isOversized INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is oversized., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isPromo INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a promotional printing., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isReprint INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has been reprinted., Column Value Explanation: 0: has not 1: has not been,
    isReserved INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is on the Magic: The Gathering Reserved List (opens new window), Column Value Explanation: If the card is on the Magic, it will appear in The Gathering Reserved List,
    isStarter INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isStorySpotlight INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a Story Spotlight card., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isTextless INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card does not have a text box., Column Value Explanation: 0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;,
    isTimeshifted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is time shifted, Column Value Explanation: If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion.,
    keywords TEXT -- Column Description: A list of keywords found on the card.,
    layout TEXT -- Column Description: The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token",
    leadershipSkills TEXT -- Column Description: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in,
    life TEXT -- Column Description: The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.,
    loyalty TEXT -- Column Description: The starting loyalty value of the card., Column Value Explanation: Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown,
    manaCost TEXT -- Column Description: The mana cost of the card wrapped in brackets for each value., Column Value Explanation: manaCost is unconverted mana cost,
    mcmId TEXT,
    mcmMetaId TEXT,
    mtgArenaId TEXT,
    mtgjsonV4Id TEXT,
    mtgoFoilId TEXT,
    mtgoId TEXT,
    multiverseId TEXT,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the card., Column Value Explanation: Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.,
    number TEXT -- Column Description: The number of the card,
    originalReleaseDate TEXT -- Column Description: original Release Date, Column Value Explanation: The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions.,
    originalText TEXT -- Column Description: original Text, Column Value Explanation: The text on the card as originally printed.,
    originalType TEXT -- Column Description: original Type, Column Value Explanation: The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    otherFaceIds TEXT -- Column Description: other Face Ids, Column Value Explanation: A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces.,
    power TEXT -- Column Description: The power of the card., Column Value Explanation: ∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power,
    printings TEXT -- Column Description: A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.,
    promoTypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of promotional types for a card., Column Value Explanation: "arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork",
    purchaseUrls TEXT -- Column Description: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.,
    rarity TEXT -- Column Description: The card printing rarity.,
    scryfallId TEXT,
    scryfallIllustrationId TEXT,
    scryfallOracleId TEXT,
    setCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set printing code that the card is from.,
    side TEXT -- Column Description: The identifier of the card side., Column Value Explanation: Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card.,
    subtypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.,
    supertypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash., Column Value Explanation: list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes,
    tcgplayerProductId TEXT,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The rules text of the card.,
    toughness TEXT -- Column Description: The toughness of the card.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes., Column Value Explanation: "Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant",
    types TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.,
    uuid TEXT NOT NULL -- Column Description: The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.,
    variations TEXT,
    watermark TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the watermark on the card.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE foreign_data (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id number identifying this row of data,
    flavorText TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign flavor text of the card.,
    language TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign language of card.,
    multiverseid INTEGER -- Column Description: The foreign multiverse identifier of the card.,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign name of the card.,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign text ruling of the card.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The foreign type of the card. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_foreign_data_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);

CREATE TABLE sets (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this set,
    baseSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The number of cards in the set.,
    block TEXT -- Column Description: The block name the set was in.,
    booster TEXT -- Column Description: A breakdown of possibilities and weights of cards in a booster pack.,
    code TEXT NOT NULL -- Column Description: The set code for the set.,
    isFoilOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in foil.,
    isForeignOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is available only outside the United States of America.,
    isNonFoilOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in non-foil.,
    isOnlineOnly INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is only available in online game variations.,
    isPartialPreview INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the set is still in preview (spoiled). Preview sets do not have complete data.,
    keyruneCode TEXT -- Column Description: The matching Keyrune code for set image icons.,
    mcmId INTEGER -- Column Description: The Magic Card Marketset identifier.,
    mcmIdExtras INTEGER -- Column Description: The split Magic Card Market set identifier if a set is printed in two sets. This identifier represents the second set's identifier.,
    mcmName TEXT,
    mtgoCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set code for the set as it appears on Magic: The Gathering Online, Column Value Explanation: if the value is null or empty, then it doesn't appear on Magic: The Gathering Online,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the set.,
    parentCode TEXT -- Column Description: The parent set code for set variations like promotions, guild kits, etc.,
    releaseDate DATE -- Column Description: The release date in ISO 8601 format for the set.,
    tcgplayerGroupId INTEGER -- Column Description: The group identifier of the set on TCGplayer,
    totalSetSize INTEGER -- Column Description: The total number of cards in the set, including promotional and related supplemental products but excluding Alchemy modifications - however those cards are included in the set itself.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The expansion type of the set., Column Value Explanation: "alchemy", "archenemy", "arsenal", "box", "commander", "core", "draft_innovation", "duel_deck", "expansion", "from_the_vault", "funny", "masterpiece", "masters", "memorabilia", "planechase", "premium_deck", "promo", "spellbook", "starter", "token", "treasure_chest", "vanguard",
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the cards belonging to the 'Coldsnap' set. 2) Determine the highest converted mana cost among those cards. 3) Retrieve the Italian names of the cards with that highest converted mana cost. The set name is needed to filter for the 'Coldsnap' set. The convertedManaCost is needed to find the maximum value. The name column in foreign_data table is needed to retrieve the Italian names. The language column in foreign_data table is needed to filter for Italian names. The cards.id and foreign_data.uuid are needed to join the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = ( SELECT MAX(T2_sub.convertedManaCost) FROM cards AS T2_sub INNER JOIN sets AS T3_sub ON T2_sub.setCode = T3_sub.code WHERE T3_sub.name = 'Coldsnap' )

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM foreign_data AS T1 INNER JOIN cards AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid INNER JOIN sets AS T3 ON T2.setCode = T3.code WHERE T1.language = 'Italian' AND T3.name = 'Coldsnap' AND T2.convertedManaCost = ( SELECT MAX(T4.convertedManaCost) FROM cards AS T4 INNER JOIN sets AS T5 ON T4.setCode = T5.code WHERE T5.name = 'Coldsnap' )

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the cards belonging to the 'Coldsnap' set. 2) Determine the highest converted mana cost among those cards. 3) Retrieve the Italian names of the cards with that highest converted mana cost. The set name is needed to filter for the 'Coldsnap' set. The convertedManaCost is needed to find the maximum value. The name column in foreign_data table is needed to retrieve the Italian names. selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Filter cards that do not have multiple faces (implied by layout), 2) Find the card with the highest converted mana cost, and 3) Retrieve the artist of that card. The layout column is needed to filter for cards that do not have multiple faces. The convertedManaCost column is needed to find the highest converted mana cost. The artist column is needed to retrieve the illustrator's name. The id column is needed to uniquely identify the cards.

The question asks for the illustrator (artist) of the card art that has the highest converted mana cost, with the condition that the card does not have multiple faces. 

1. **Filtering for cards without multiple faces:** The schema description for the `cards` table mentions `layout` TEXT with an explanation: 'The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"'. It also has a column `isTextless` which is an integer. The hint mentions 'doesn't have multiple faces refers to side IS NULL'. However, there is no 'side' column in the schema. Looking at the `layout` column, 'Split' and 'Meld' cards are mentioned as examples of cards with multiple faces. Therefore, to exclude cards with multiple faces, I should filter where the `layout` is not 'split' and not 'meld'. If the `layout` column is NULL, it implies it's not a special layout like split or meld, so filtering for `layout IS NULL` might be a way to interpret 'no multiple faces'. However, the provided schema does not have a `side` column. Given the examples in the schema description for `cards.name` ('Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.'), it's more likely that the `layout` column is what distinguishes these. The hint 'side IS NULL' is likely a misdirection or refers to a column not present. I will assume that cards with `layout` other than 'split' and 'meld' are considered single-faced. If `layout` is NULL, it's also a single-faced card. So, I need to filter `layout` to exclude 'split' and 'meld'. 

2. **Identifying the highest converted mana cost:** The `convertedManaCost` column in the `cards` table stores the converted mana cost. To find the highest cost, I need to use an aggregation function like `MAX()` or order by this column in descending order and take the top one. 

3. **Identifying the illustrator:** The `artist` column in the `cards` table stores the name of the illustrator. This is the value that needs to be returned.

Therefore, I need the `artist`, `convertedManaCost`, and `layout` columns from the `cards` table.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT "artist" FROM "cards" WHERE "side" IS NULL ORDER BY "convertedManaCost" DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

The artist column is needed to retrieve the illustrator's name. The id column is needed to uniquely identify the cards.

Execution plan: The question asks for the illustrator (artist) of the card art that has the highest converted mana cost, with the condition that the card does not have multiple faces. 

1. **Filtering for cards without multiple faces:** The schema description for the `cards` table mentions `layout` TEXT with an explanation: 'The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token"'. It also has a column `isTextless` which is an integer. The hint mentions 'doesn't have multiple faces refers to side IS NULL'. However, there is no 'side' column in the schema. Looking at the `layout` column, 'Split' and 'Meld' cards are mentioned as examples of cards with multiple faces. Therefore, to exclude cards with multiple faces, I should filter where the `layout` is not 'split' and not 'meld'. If the `layout` column is NULL, it implies it's not a special layout like split or meld, so filtering for `layout IS NULL` might be a way to interpret 'no multiple faces'. However, the provided schema does not have a `side` column. Given the examples in the schema description for `cards.name` ('Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.'), it's more likely that the `layout` column is what distinguishes these. The hint 'side IS NULL' is likely a misdirection or refers to a column not present. I will assume that cards with `layout` other than 'split' and 'meld' are considered single-faced. If `layout` is NULL, it's also a single-faced card. So, I need to filter `layout` to exclude 'split' and 'meld'. 

2. **Identifying the highest converted mana cost:** The `convertedManaCost` column in the `cards` table stores the converted mana cost. To find the highest cost, I need to use an aggregation function like `MAX()` or order by this column in descending order and take the top one. 

3. **Identifying the illustrator:** The `artist` column in the `cards` table stores the name of the illustrator. This is the value that needs to be returned.

Therefore, I need the `artist`, `convertedManaCost`, and `layout` columns from the `cards` table.

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to find the oldest mythic card, which requires filtering by rarity and finding the minimum release date. Then, I need to determine the legal play formats for that card. The originalReleaseDate column is needed to find the oldest card. The rarity column is needed to filter for mythic cards. The format and status columns from the legalities table are needed to determine the legal play formats. The cards table needs to be joined with the legalities table to find the legal formats for the card. The uuid is needed to join cards and legalities tables.

The question asks for the release year of the oldest 'mythic' rarity card and its legal play formats. 

1. To find the 'oldest' card, I need to look at the `originalReleaseDate` column in the `cards` table and find the minimum value. The question specifically asks for the release YEAR, so I'll need to extract the year from this date.
2. The question specifies 'mythic card', so I need to filter the `cards` table using the `rarity` column where `rarity = 'mythic'`.
3. To find the 'legal play formats', I need to join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using a common identifier. The `legalities` table contains `format` and `status` columns. I need to filter for `status = 'legal'`.
4. The `uuid` column is the primary key in `cards` and is used as a foreign key in `legalities` to link cards to their legalities, so it's essential for the join.

Therefore, the essential columns are: `cards.originalReleaseDate` (for finding the oldest date and extracting the year), `cards.rarity` (for filtering mythic cards), `cards.uuid` (for joining with `legalities`), `legalities.uuid` (for joining with `cards`), `legalities.status` (for filtering legal formats), and `legalities.format` (to display the legal formats).

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1."originalReleaseDate", T2."format" FROM "cards" AS T1 INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2 ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid" WHERE T1."uuid" = (SELECT "uuid" FROM "cards" WHERE "rarity" = 'mythic' ORDER BY "originalReleaseDate" ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1) AND T2."status" = 'Legal'

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
          T1."originalReleaseDate",
          T2."format"
        FROM "cards" AS T1
        INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
          ON T1."uuid" = T2."uuid"
        WHERE
          T1."uuid" = (
            SELECT
              "uuid"
            FROM "cards"
            WHERE
              "rarity" = 'mythic'
            ORDER BY
              "originalReleaseDate" ASC NULLS LAST
            LIMIT 1
          ) AND T2."status" = 'Legal';

Execution plan: The question asks for the release year of the oldest 'mythic' rarity card and its legal play formats. 

1. To find the 'oldest' card, I need to look at the `originalReleaseDate` column in the `cards` table and find the minimum value. The question specifically asks for the release YEAR, so I'll need to extract the year from this date.
2. The question specifies 'mythic card', so I need to filter the `cards` table using the `rarity` column where `rarity = 'mythic'`.
3. To find the 'legal play formats', I need to join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using a common identifier. The `legalities` table contains `format` and `status` columns. I need to filter for `status = 'legal'`.
4. The `uuid` column is the primary key in `cards` and is used as a foreign key in `legalities` to link cards to their legalities, so it's essential for the join.

Therefore, the essential columns are: `cards.originalReleaseDate` (for finding the oldest date and extracting the year), `cards.rarity` (for filtering mythic cards), `cards.uuid` (for joining with `legalities`), `legalities.uuid` (for joining with `cards`), `legalities.status` (for filtering legal formats), and `legalities.format` (to display the legal formats).

SELECT
  T1.originalReleaseDate,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.uuid = (
    SELECT
      uuid
    FROM cards
    WHERE
      rarity = 'mythic'
    ORDER BY
      originalReleaseDate ASC
    LIMIT 1
  ) AND T2.status = 'legal';

1. To find the 'oldest' card, I need to look at the `originalReleaseDate` column in the `cards` table and find the minimum value. The question specifically asks for the release YEAR, so I'll need to extract the year from this date.
2. The question specifies 'mythic card', so I need to filter the `cards` table using the `rarity` column where `rarity = 'mythic'`.
3. To find the 'legal play formats', I need to join the `cards` table with the `legalities` table using a common identifier. The `legalities` table contains `format` and `status` columns. I need to filter for `status = 'legal'`.
4. The `uuid` column is the primary key in `cards` and is used as a foreign key in `legalities` to link cards to their legalities, so it's essential for the join.

Therefore, the essential columns are: `cards.originalReleaseDate` (for finding the oldest date and extracting the year), `cards.rarity` (for filtering mythic cards), `cards.uuid` (for joining with `legalities`), `legalities.uuid` (for joining with `cards`), `legalities.status` (for filtering legal formats), and `legalities.format` (to display the legal formats).

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT
  T1.originalReleaseDate,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE
  T1.rarity = 'mythic' AND T2.status = 'legal' AND T1.originalReleaseDate = (
    SELECT
      MIN(originalReleaseDate)
    FROM cards
    WHERE
      rarity = 'mythic'
  );

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards, which requires counting cards per artist. 2) Determine the formats those cards belong to. The artist column is needed for counting illustrators. The id column is needed to join with legalities. The format column is needed to list the play formats.

The question asks to identify the illustrator with the least amount of cards and list the formats of play for the cards they illustrated. This requires joining the 'cards' table (to get the artist and card information) with the 'legalities' table (to get the format of play). First, I need to count the number of cards illustrated by each artist. This involves grouping by 'artist' in the 'cards' table and using COUNT(id). Then, I need to find the artist with the minimum count. After identifying this artist, I need to retrieve all the distinct formats of play associated with the cards illustrated by this artist. This requires joining 'cards' and 'legalities' on the card's unique identifier (which is 'id' in 'cards' and implicitly linked via 'uuid' in 'foreign_data', 'legalities', 'rulings', and 'set_translations' to 'cards.id', assuming 'uuid' in those tables corresponds to 'cards.id'). Since 'legalities' has a 'format' column and a 'uuid' column that links to 'cards', I will use these. The criteria specify returning distinct formats, so I will use DISTINCT on the format column. Therefore, I need 'cards.id', 'cards.artist', 'legalities.uuid', and 'legalities.format'. The criteria also states that the format of play refers to 'format', and illustrator refers to 'artist'. The least amount of cards refers to MIN(artist), which implies finding the artist with the minimum count of cards. The output should be the format of play, distinct. So, I need 'cards.artist' for filtering and grouping, 'cards.id' to join with 'legalities', and 'legalities.uuid' to link to 'cards.id', and 'legalities.format' for the output and to ensure it's associated with the correct cards.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist IN (SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(id) = (SELECT MIN(card_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(id) AS card_count FROM cards GROUP BY artist)))

The artist column is needed for counting illustrators. The id column is needed to join with legalities. The format column is needed to list the play formats.

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH ArtistCardCounts AS (
    SELECT
        artist,
        COUNT(id) AS card_count
    FROM cards
    WHERE artist IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY artist
), MinCardCount AS (
    SELECT MIN(card_count) AS min_count
    FROM ArtistCardCounts
)
SELECT DISTINCT
    T1.artist,
    T3.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN ArtistCardCounts AS T2
    ON T1.artist = T2.artist
INNER JOIN MinCardCount AS T_min
    ON T2.card_count = T_min.min_count
INNER JOIN legalities AS T3
    ON T1.uuid = T3.uuid

    isFullArt INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card has full artwork., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have, 1: has full artwork,

    isStarter INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is found in a starter deck such as Planeswalker/Brawl decks., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isStorySpotlight INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is a Story Spotlight card., Column Value Explanation: 0: is not 1: is,
    isTextless INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card does not have a text box., Column Value Explanation: 0: has a text box; 1: doesn't have a text box;,
    isTimeshifted INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 -- Column Description: If the card is time shifted, Column Value Explanation: If the card is "timeshifted", a feature of certain sets where a card will have a different frameVersion.,
    keywords TEXT -- Column Description: A list of keywords found on the card.,
    layout TEXT -- Column Description: The type of card layout. For a token card, this will be "token",
    leadershipSkills TEXT -- Column Description: A list of formats the card is legal to be a commander in,
    life TEXT -- Column Description: The starting life total modifier. A plus or minus character precedes an integer.,
    loyalty TEXT -- Column Description: The starting loyalty value of the card., Column Value Explanation: Used only on cards with "Planeswalker" in its types. empty means unkown,

    mtgjsonV4Id TEXT,
    mtgoFoilId TEXT,
    mtgoId TEXT,
    multiverseId TEXT,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the card., Column Value Explanation: Cards with multiple faces, like "Split" and "Meld" cards are given a delimiter.,
    number TEXT -- Column Description: The number of the card,
    originalReleaseDate TEXT -- Column Description: original Release Date, Column Value Explanation: The original release date in ISO 8601(opens new window) format for a promotional card printed outside of a cycle window, such as Secret Lair Drop promotions.,
    originalText TEXT -- Column Description: original Text, Column Value Explanation: The text on the card as originally printed.,
    originalType TEXT -- Column Description: original Type, Column Value Explanation: The type of the card as originally printed. Includes any supertypes and subtypes.,
    otherFaceIds TEXT -- Column Description: other Face Ids, Column Value Explanation: A list of card UUID's to this card's counterparts, such as transformed or melded faces.,
    power TEXT -- Column Description: The power of the card., Column Value Explanation: ∞ means infinite power null or * refers to unknown power,
    printings TEXT -- Column Description: A list of set printing codes the card was printed in, formatted in uppercase.,
    promoTypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of promotional types for a card., Column Value Explanation: "arenaleague", "boosterfun", "boxtopper", "brawldeck", "bundle", "buyabox", "convention", "datestamped", "draculaseries", "draftweekend", "duels", "event", "fnm", "gameday", "gateway", "giftbox", "gilded", "godzillaseries", "instore", "intropack", "jpwalker", "judgegift", "league", "mediainsert", "neonink", "openhouse", "planeswalkerstamped", "playerrewards", "playpromo", "premiereshop", "prerelease", "promopack", "release", "setpromo", "stamped", "textured", "themepack", "thick", "tourney", "wizardsplaynetwork",
    purchaseUrls TEXT -- Column Description: Links that navigate to websites where the card can be purchased.,
    rarity TEXT -- Column Description: The card printing rarity.,
    scryfallId TEXT,
    scryfallIllustrationId TEXT,
    scryfallOracleId TEXT,
    setCode TEXT -- Column Description: The set printing code that the card is from.,
    side TEXT -- Column Description: The identifier of the card side., Column Value Explanation: Used on cards with multiple faces on the same card.  if this value is empty, then it means this card doesn't have multiple faces on the same card.,
    subtypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card subtypes found after em-dash.,
    supertypes TEXT -- Column Description: A list of card supertypes found before em-dash., Column Value Explanation: list of all types should be the union of subtypes and supertypes,
    tcgplayerProductId TEXT,
    text TEXT -- Column Description: The rules text of the card.,
    toughness TEXT -- Column Description: The toughness of the card.,
    type TEXT -- Column Description: The type of the card as visible, including any supertypes and subtypes., Column Value Explanation: "Artifact", "Card", "Conspiracy", "Creature", "Dragon", "Dungeon", "Eaturecray", "Elemental", "Elite", "Emblem", "Enchantment", "Ever", "Goblin", "Hero", "Instant", "Jaguar", "Knights", "Land", "Phenomenon", "Plane", "Planeswalker", "Scariest", "Scheme", "See", "Sorcery", "Sticker", "Summon", "Token", "Tribal", "Vanguard", "Wolf", "You’ll", "instant",
    types TEXT -- Column Description: A list of all card types of the card, including Un‑sets and gameplay variants.,
    uuid TEXT NOT NULL -- Column Description: The universal unique identifier (v5) generated by MTGJSON. Each entry is unique.,
    variations TEXT,
    watermark TEXT -- Column Description: The name of the watermark on the card.,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE legalities (

    id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: unique id identifying this legality,
    format TEXT -- Column Description: format of play, Column Value Explanation: each value refers to different rules to play,
    status TEXT -- , Column Value Explanation: • legal • banned • restricted,
    uuid TEXT,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_legalities_uuid FOREIGN KEY (uuid) REFERENCES cards (uuid)

);
schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: The question asks to identify the illustrator with the least amount of cards and list the formats of play for the cards they illustrated. This requires joining the 'cards' table (to get the artist and card information) with the 'legalities' table (to get the format of play). First, I need to count the number of cards illustrated by each artist. This involves grouping by 'artist' in the 'cards' table and using COUNT(id). Then, I need to find the artist with the minimum count. After identifying this artist, I need to retrieve all the distinct formats of play associated with the cards illustrated by this artist. This requires joining 'cards' and 'legalities' on the card's unique identifier (which is 'id' in 'cards' and implicitly linked via 'uuid' in 'foreign_data', 'legalities', 'rulings', and 'set_translations' to 'cards.id', assuming 'uuid' in those tables corresponds to 'cards.id'). Since 'legalities' has a 'format' column and a 'uuid' column that links to 'cards', I will use these. The criteria specify returning distinct formats, so I will use DISTINCT on the format column. Therefore, I need 'cards.id', 'cards.artist', 'legalities.uuid', and 'legalities.format'. The criteria also states that the format of play refers to 'format', and illustrator refers to 'artist'. The least amount of cards refers to MIN(artist), which implies finding the artist with the minimum count of cards. The output should be the format of play, distinct. So, I need 'cards.artist' for filtering and grouping, 'cards.id' to join with 'legalities', and 'legalities.uuid' to link to 'cards.id', and 'legalities.format' for the output and to ensure it's associated with the correct cards.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist = (SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist ORDER BY COUNT(id) ASC LIMIT 1)

SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.artist,
  T2.format
FROM cards AS T1
INNER JOIN legalities AS T2
  ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid
WHERE T1.artist = (
    SELECT artist
    FROM cards
    WHERE artist IS NOT NULL AND artist != ''
    GROUP BY artist
    ORDER BY COUNT(id) ASC
    LIMIT 1
);

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the artist who illustrated the least amount of cards, which requires counting cards per artist. 2) Determine the formats those cards belong to. The artist column is needed for counting illustrators. The id column is needed to join with legalities. The format column is needed to list the play formats.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT T1."artist", T2."format"
FROM "cards" AS T1
INNER JOIN "legalities" AS T2
  ON T1."id" = T2."uuid"
WHERE
  T1."artist" = (
    SELECT
      "artist"
    FROM "cards"
    GROUP BY
      "artist"
    ORDER BY
      COUNT("id") ASC
    LIMIT 1
  );

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T2.format FROM cards AS T1 INNER JOIN legalities AS T2 ON T1.uuid = T2.uuid WHERE T1.artist IN (SELECT artist FROM cards GROUP BY artist HAVING COUNT(id) = (SELECT MIN(card_count) FROM (SELECT COUNT(id) AS card_count FROM cards GROUP BY artist)))

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to find sets that have Korean translations but not Japanese translations. This involves checking the 'name' of the set and filtering based on the 'language' in the 'set_translations' table. The 'sets' table is needed to get the set names. The 'set_translations' table is needed to filter by language. The 'name' column from the 'sets' table is needed to display the result. The 'language' column from the 'set_translations' table is needed to filter by language.

The question asks to find set names that have Korean translations but do not have Japanese translations. This requires joining the `sets` table with the `set_translations` table to access translation information. Specifically, I need to filter `set_translations` by `language` to identify sets with Korean translations and exclude those with Japanese translations. The `sets.name` column is needed to output the names of the qualifying sets. The `set_translations.translation` column is not directly needed as the filtering is based on the `language` column, and the `sets.id` and `set_translations.setCode` are foreign keys needed for the join.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.name FROM sets AS T1 WHERE T1.code IN ( SELECT DISTINCT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Korean' ) AND T1.code NOT IN ( SELECT DISTINCT setCode FROM set_translations WHERE language = 'Japanese' )

See this official article (opens new window) for more information., Column Value Explanation: 0: doesn't have 1: has sensitve content or Wizards of the Coast  Cards with this property may have missing or degraded properties and values.,

CREATE TABLE posts (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the post id,
    PostTypeId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the post type,
    AcceptedAnswerId INTEGER -- Column Description: the accepted answer id of the post,
    CreaionDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the post,
    Score INTEGER -- Column Description: the score of the post,
    ViewCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the view count of the post, Column Value Explanation: Higher view count means the post has higher popularity,
    Body TEXT -- Column Description: the body of the post,
    OwnerUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the owner user,
    LasActivityDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last activity date,
    Title TEXT -- Column Description: the title of the post,
    Tags TEXT -- Column Description: the tag of the post,
    AnswerCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of answers of the post,
    CommentCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of comments of the post,
    FavoriteCount INTEGER -- Column Description: the total number of favorites of the post, Column Value Explanation: more favorite count refers to more valuable posts.,
    LastEditorUserId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the last editor,
    LastEditDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last edit date,
    CommunityOwnedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the community owned date,
    ParentId INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the parent post, Column Value Explanation: If the parent id is null, the post is the root post. Otherwise, the post is the child post of other post.,
    ClosedDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the closed date of the post, Column Value Explanation: if ClosedDate is null or empty, it means this post is not well-finished if CloseDate is not null or empty, it means this post has well-finished.,
    OwnerDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the post owner,
    LastEditorDisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the display name of the last editor,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_LastEditorUserId FOREIGN KEY (LastEditorUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_OwnerUserId FOREIGN KEY (OwnerUserId) REFERENCES users (Id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_posts_ParentId FOREIGN KEY (ParentId) REFERENCES posts (Id)

);

CREATE TABLE users (

    Id INTEGER NOT NULL -- Column Description: the user id,
    Reputation INTEGER -- Column Description: the user's reputation, Column Value Explanation: The user with higher reputation has more influence.,
    CreationDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the creation date of the user account,
    DisplayName TEXT -- Column Description: the user's display name,
    LastAccessDate DATETIME -- Column Description: the last access date of the user account,
    WebsiteUrl TEXT -- Column Description: the website url of the user account,
    Location TEXT -- Column Description: user's location,
    AboutMe TEXT -- Column Description: the self introduction of the user,
    Views INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of views,
    UpVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of upvotes,
    DownVotes INTEGER -- Column Description: the number of downvotes,
    AccountId INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id of the account,
    Age INTEGER -- Column Description: user's age, Column Value Explanation:  teenager: 13-18  adult: 19-65  elder: > 65,
    ProfileImageUrl TEXT -- Column Description: the profile image url,
    PRIMARY KEY (Id)

);

The question asks for the display name and website URL of the user who received the highest bounty amount for a vote type of 8. 

1. **Filtering by Vote Type:** The `votes` table contains `VoteTypeId` and `BountyAmount`. I need to filter for `VoteTypeId = 8`.
2. **Finding the Highest Bounty Amount:** I need to find the maximum `BountyAmount` within the filtered votes. This requires the `BountyAmount` column from the `votes` table.
3. **Identifying the User:** The `votes` table has a `UserId` column, which links to the `users` table. I need this `UserId` to find the corresponding user.
4. **Retrieving User Information:** The `users` table contains `DisplayName` and `WebsiteUrl`, which are the required output fields. It also has `Id` which is the primary key and foreign key to `votes.UserId`.

The question asks for the full name of the tallest hero published by 'Marvel Comics'. To answer this, I need to: 1. Join the `superhero` table with the `publisher` table to filter for 'Marvel Comics'. 2. Identify the hero with the maximum `height_cm` within the filtered results. 3. Return the `full_name` of that hero. Therefore, I need `publisher_name` from the `publisher` table to filter for 'Marvel Comics', `height_cm` from the `superhero` table to find the tallest hero, and `full_name` from the `superhero` table to display the result. The `superhero.id` and `publisher.id` are needed for the join operation.

sql_exec_info.sql:
SELECT "T1"."full_name"
FROM "superhero" AS "T1"
INNER JOIN "publisher" AS "T2"
  ON "T1"."publisher_id" = "T2"."id"
WHERE
  "T2"."publisher_name" = 'Marvel Comics' AND "T1"."height_cm" > 0
ORDER BY
  "T1"."height_cm" DESC
LIMIT 1;

The question asks for the eyes, hair, and skin colour of female superheroes published by Dark Horse Comics. This requires joining the `superhero` table with `gender`, `publisher`, and `colour` tables. 

1. **Filtering for 'Female' superheroes:** I need to join `superhero` with `gender` and filter where `gender.gender` is 'Female'. This means I need `superhero.gender_id` and `gender.id`, `gender.gender`.
2. **Filtering for 'Dark Horse Comics' publishers:** I need to join `superhero` with `publisher` and filter where `publisher.publisher_name` is 'Dark Horse Comics'. This means I need `superhero.publisher_id` and `publisher.id`, `publisher.publisher_name`.
3. **Retrieving colour information:** The question asks for eyes, hair, and skin colour. These are linked via `superhero.eye_colour_id`, `superhero.hair_colour_id`, and `superhero.skin_colour_id`. These `id`s will need to be joined with the `colour` table to get the actual colour names. So, I need `superhero.eye_colour_id`, `superhero.hair_colour_id`, `superhero.skin_colour_id`, and `colour.id`, `colour.colour`.

Therefore, the essential columns are: `superhero.id` (for joining), `superhero.gender_id`, `gender.gender`, `superhero.publisher_id`, `publisher.publisher_name`, `superhero.eye_colour_id`, `superhero.hair_colour_id`, `superhero.skin_colour_id`, and `colour.colour` (to display the actual colour names).

SELECT
  T_eye.colour,
  T_hair.colour,
  T_skin.colour
FROM superhero AS T1
INNER JOIN publisher AS T2

INNER JOIN gender AS T3
  ON T1.gender_id = T3.id
LEFT JOIN colour AS T_eye

WHERE

);

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH AustralianGP AS (
  SELECT "raceId"
  FROM "races"
  WHERE "year" = 2008 AND "name" = 'Australian Grand Prix'
),
RaceResults AS (
  SELECT
    "positionOrder",
    "milliseconds"
  FROM "results"
  WHERE "raceId" = (SELECT "raceId" FROM AustralianGP)
    AND "milliseconds" IS NOT NULL
),
ChampionTime AS (
  SELECT "milliseconds" AS champion_ms
  FROM RaceResults
  WHERE "positionOrder" = 1
),
LastDriverTime AS (
  SELECT "milliseconds" AS last_driver_ms
  FROM RaceResults
  ORDER BY "positionOrder" DESC
  LIMIT 1
)
SELECT
  ((SELECT last_driver_ms FROM LastDriverTime) - (SELECT champion_ms FROM ChampionTime)) * 100.0 / (SELECT last_driver_ms FROM LastDriverTime)

WITH TargetRace AS (
  SELECT
    raceId
  FROM races
  WHERE
    name = 'Australian Grand Prix' AND year = 2008
), ChampionTime AS (
  SELECT
    T1.milliseconds AS champion_ms
  FROM results AS T1
  INNER JOIN TargetRace AS T2
    ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId
  WHERE
    T1.position = 1
), LastDriverTime AS (
  SELECT
    T1.milliseconds AS last_driver_ms
  FROM results AS T1
  INNER JOIN TargetRace AS T2
    ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId
  WHERE
    T1.milliseconds IS NOT NULL
  ORDER BY
    T1.position DESC
  LIMIT 1
)

  (
    (LDT.last_driver_ms - CT.champion_ms) * 100.0 / LDT.last_driver_ms
  )
FROM ChampionTime AS CT,
  LastDriverTime AS LDT;

The hint suggests that the time is not null for finished drivers. I need to join the tables to get the driver's time. The race id is needed to filter by the 2008 Australian Grand Prix. The driverRef is needed to identify the driver.

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH AustralianGP_Race AS (
  -- Sub-question 1: Get the raceId for 'Australian Grand Prix'.
  -- We use LIMIT 1 to ensure a single raceId is selected, assuming the question implies a unique race.
  SELECT "raceId"
  FROM "races"
  WHERE "name" = 'Australian Grand Prix'
  LIMIT 1
),
FinishedDriversForRace AS (
  -- Combine results and lapTimes for the identified race and convert times to seconds.
  -- Filter for drivers who finished (time IS NOT NULL).
  SELECT
    T1.driverId,
    T1.position,
    (CAST(SUBSTR(T2.time, 1, INSTR(T2.time, ':') - 1) AS REAL) * 60 + CAST(SUBSTR(T2.time, INSTR(T2.time, ':') + 1) AS REAL)) AS time_in_seconds
  FROM "results" AS T1
  INNER JOIN "lapTimes" AS T2
    ON T1.raceId = T2.raceId AND T1.driverId = T2.driverId
  WHERE
    T1.raceId = (SELECT "raceId" FROM AustralianGP_Race)
    AND T2.time IS NOT NULL
),
Champion AS (
  -- Sub-question 2: Get the champion's time in seconds.
  SELECT time_in_seconds
  FROM FinishedDriversForRace
  WHERE position = 1
),
LastDriver AS (
  -- Sub-question 3: Get the last-place driver's time in seconds.
  -- Sub-question 3.1 is embedded here to find the MAX position among finished drivers.
  SELECT time_in_seconds
  FROM FinishedDriversForRace
  WHERE position = (SELECT MAX(position) FROM FinishedDriversForRace)
)
-- Main Question: Calculate the percentage difference.
SELECT
  ((L.time_in_seconds - C.time_in_seconds) * 100.0 / L.time_in_seconds)
FROM Champion AS C, LastDriver AS L;

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To calculate the percentage difference in speed, I need to determine the champion's time and the last-place finisher's time in the 2008 Australian Grand Prix. The hint suggests that the time is not null for finished drivers. I need to join the tables to get the driver's time. The race id is needed to filter by the 2008 Australian Grand Prix. The driverRef is needed to identify the driver.

sql_exec_info.sql:
WITH RaceResult AS (
  SELECT
    r.raceId,
    r.name AS raceName
  FROM races AS r
  WHERE
    r.name = '2008 Australian Grand Prix'
), Champion AS (
  SELECT
    res.driverId,
    res.position
  FROM results AS res
  JOIN RaceResult AS rr ON res.raceId = rr.raceId
  WHERE
    res.position = 1
), LastPlace AS (
  SELECT
    res.driverId,
    res.position
  FROM results AS res
  JOIN RaceResult AS rr ON res.raceId = rr.raceId
  WHERE
    res.position = (
      SELECT
        MAX(position)
      FROM results
      WHERE
        raceId = (
          SELECT
            raceId
          FROM RaceResult
        )
    )

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: The question requires filtering teams based on their buildUpPlaySpeed and displaying their team_fifa_api_id. Therefore, I need to access the buildUpPlaySpeed column for filtering and the team_fifa_api_id for output. These columns are found within the Team_Attributes table.

The question asks for the `team_fifa_api_id` of teams that have a `buildUpPlaySpeed` between 50 and 60. The hint specifies that this range should be interpreted as `BETWEEN 51 AND 59`. Therefore, I need to select the `team_fifa_api_id` from the `Team_Attributes` table and filter based on the `buildUpPlaySpeed` column in the same table. The `Team` table is not needed as the `team_fifa_api_id` is directly available in `Team_Attributes` and no other information from the `Team` table is requested.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT "team_fifa_api_id" FROM "Team_Attributes" WHERE "buildUpPlaySpeed" BETWEEN 51 AND 59

The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed to calculate the average and filter the teams. The team_long_name is needed to display the required output. The Team_Attributes table is needed to get the buildUpPlayPassing and the Team table is needed to get the team_long_name. The question doesn't mention any date-related filtering, so the date column is not needed.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.team_long_name FROM Team AS T1 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id WHERE T2.buildUpPlayPassing > ( SELECT AVG(buildUpPlayPassing) FROM Team_Attributes WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012' AND buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL ) AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012'

CREATE TABLE Player (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    player_name TEXT -- Column Description: player name,
    player_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player fifa api,
    birthday TEXT -- Column Description: the player's birthday, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 1992-02-29 00:00:00  commonsense reasoning:  Player A is older than player B means that A's birthday is earlier than B's,
    height INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's height,
    weight INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's weight,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Player_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for players,
    player_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player fifa api,
    player_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the player api,
    date TEXT -- Column Description: date, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2016-02-18 00:00:00,
    overall_rating INTEGER -- Column Description: the overall rating of the player, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The rating is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher overall rating means the player has a stronger overall strength.,
    potential INTEGER -- Column Description: potential of the player, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The potential score is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher potential score means that the player has more potential,
    preferred_foot TEXT -- Column Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking, Column Value Explanation: right/ left,
    attacking_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's attacking work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks,
    defensive_work_rate TEXT -- Column Description: the player's defensive work rate, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: remain in his position and defense while the team attacks  • medium: implies that the player will select the defensive actions he will join in • low: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves instead of defensing,
    crossing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's crossing score, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  Cross is a long pass into the opponent's goal towards the header of sixth-yard teammate.  The crossing score is between 0-100 which measures the tendency/frequency of crosses in the box.  Higher potential score means that the player performs better in crossing actions.,
    finishing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's finishing rate, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    heading_accuracy INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's heading accuracy, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    short_passing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's short passing score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    volleys INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's volley score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    dribbling INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's dribbling score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    curve INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's curve score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    free_kick_accuracy INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's free kick accuracy, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    long_passing INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's long passing score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    ball_control INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's ball control score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    acceleration INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's acceleration score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sprint_speed INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sprint speed, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    agility INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's agility, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    reactions INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's reactions score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    balance INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's balance score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    shot_power INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's shot power, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    jumping INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's jumping score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    stamina INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's stamina score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    strength INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's strength score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    long_shots INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's long shots score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    aggression INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's aggression score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    interceptions INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's interceptions score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's  positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    vision INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's vision score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    penalties INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's penalties score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    marking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's markingscore, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    standing_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's standing tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    sliding_tackle INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's sliding tackle score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_diving INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep diving score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_handling INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep diving score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_kicking INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep kicking score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_positioning INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep positioning score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    gk_reflexes INTEGER -- Column Description: the player's goalkeep reflexes score, Column Value Explanation: 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Player_Attributes_player_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (player_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Player (player_fifa_api_id)

);

CREATE TABLE Team (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for teams,
    team_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team api,
    team_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team fifa api,
    team_long_name TEXT -- Column Description: the team's long name,
    team_short_name TEXT -- Column Description: the team's short name,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Team_Attributes (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for teams,
    team_fifa_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team fifa api,
    team_api_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the id of the team api,
    date TEXT -- Column Description: Date, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2010-02-22 00:00:00,
    buildUpPlaySpeed INTEGER -- Column Description: the speed in which attacks are put together, Column Value Explanation: the score which is between 1-00 to measure the team's attack speed,
    buildUpPlaySpeedClass TEXT -- Column Description: the speed class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Slow: 1-33 • Balanced: 34-66 • Fast: 66-100,
    buildUpPlayDribbling INTEGER -- Column Description: the tendency/ frequency of dribbling,
    buildUpPlayDribblingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the dribbling class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Little: 1-33 • Normal: 34-66 • Lots: 66-100,
    buildUpPlayPassing INTEGER -- Column Description: affects passing distance and support from teammates,
    buildUpPlayPassingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the passing class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Short: 1-33 • Mixed: 34-66 • Long: 66-100,
    buildUpPlayPositioningClass TEXT -- Column Description: A team's freedom of movement in the 1st two thirds of the pitch, Column Value Explanation: Organised / Free Form,
    chanceCreationPassing INTEGER -- Column Description: Amount of risk in pass decision and run support,
    chanceCreationPassingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the chance creation passing class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Safe: 1-33 • Normal: 34-66 • Risky: 66-100,
    chanceCreationCrossing INTEGER -- Column Description: The tendency / frequency of crosses into the box,
    chanceCreationCrossingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the chance creation crossing class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Little: 1-33 • Normal: 34-66 • Lots: 66-100,
    chanceCreationShooting INTEGER -- Column Description: The tendency / frequency of shots taken,
    chanceCreationShootingClass TEXT -- Column Description: the chance creation shooting class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Little: 1-33 • Normal: 34-66 • Lots: 66-100,
    chanceCreationPositioningClass TEXT -- Column Description: A team’s freedom of movement in the final third of the pitch, Column Value Explanation: Organised / Free Form,
    defencePressure INTEGER -- Column Description: Affects how high up the pitch the team will start pressuring,
    defencePressureClass TEXT -- Column Description: the defence pressure class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Deep: 1-33 • Medium: 34-66 • High: 66-100,
    defenceAggression INTEGER -- Column Description: Affect the team’s approach to tackling the ball possessor,
    defenceAggressionClass TEXT -- Column Description: the defence aggression class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Contain: 1-33 • Press: 34-66 • Double: 66-100,
    defenceTeamWidth INTEGER -- Column Description: Affects how much the team will shift to the ball side,
    defenceTeamWidthClass TEXT -- Column Description: the defence team width class, Column Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • Narrow: 1-33 • Normal: 34-66 • Wide: 66-100,
    defenceDefenderLineClass TEXT -- Column Description: Affects the shape and strategy of the defence, Column Value Explanation: Cover/ Offside Trap,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Team_Attributes_team_api_id FOREIGN KEY (team_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_api_id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_Team_Attributes_team_fifa_api_id FOREIGN KEY (team_fifa_api_id) REFERENCES Team (team_fifa_api_id)

);

schema_representation.execution_plan: Execution plan: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Find the average buildUpPlayPassing, 2) Filter for teams with buildUpPlayPassing greater than the average, 3) Display the team's long name. The buildUpPlayPassing column is needed to calculate the average and filter the teams. The team_long_name is needed to display the required output. The Team_Attributes table is needed to get the buildUpPlayPassing and the Team table is needed to get the team_long_name. The question doesn't mention any date-related filtering, so the date column is not needed.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT DISTINCT T1.team_long_name FROM Team AS T1 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id WHERE T2.buildUpPlayPassing > ( SELECT AVG(buildUpPlayPassing) FROM Team_Attributes WHERE STRFTIME('%Y', date) = '2012' AND buildUpPlayPassing IS NOT NULL ) AND STRFTIME('%Y', T2.date) = '2012'

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer the question, I need to: 1) Filter players whose height is above 180, 2) Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player, 3) Order the players by average heading accuracy in descending order, 4) Limit the result to the top 10 players. Therefore, I need player_name and height from the Player table, and player_fifa_api_id and heading_accuracy from the Player_Attributes table. The player_fifa_api_id is needed to join the tables.

The question asks to list the names of the top 10 players whose heights are above 180, ordered by their average heading accuracy in descending order. To achieve this, I need to: 
1. Filter players based on their height being greater than 180. The `height` column in the `Player` table is required for this. 
2. Calculate the average heading accuracy for each player. The `heading_accuracy` column from the `Player_Attributes` table is needed for the sum, and `player_fifa_api_id` from `Player_Attributes` (or `Player` table, as they are linked and `player_fifa_api_id` is used in the hint for division) is needed for the count in the average calculation. 
3. Join the `Player` and `Player_Attributes` tables to link player height and their attributes. The `Player.id` and `Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id` (or `Player.player_fifa_api_id` if it exists and is the correct join key) are foreign keys that enable this join. The schema shows `Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id` references `Player.player_fifa_api_id`. 
4. Select the player's name from the `Player` table. 
5. Order the results by the calculated average heading accuracy in descending order. 
6. Limit the results to the top 10 players. 

Therefore, the essential columns are: `Player.player_name` for the output, `Player.height` for filtering, `Player_Attributes.heading_accuracy` for the average calculation, and `Player.id` and `Player_Attributes.player_fifa_api_id` for joining the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T1.player_name FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 GROUP BY T1.player_name ORDER BY AVG(T2.heading_accuracy) DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10

SELECT DISTINCT
  T1.player_name
FROM Player AS T1
INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2
  ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id
WHERE
  T1.player_name IN ('Alexis', 'Alexis Blin', 'Alexis Rolin', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone') AND T2.crossing = (
    SELECT
      MAX(T2_sub.crossing)
    FROM Player AS T1_sub
    INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2_sub
      ON T1_sub.player_api_id = T2_sub.player_api_id
    WHERE
      T1_sub.player_name IN ('Alexis', 'Alexis Blin', 'Alexis Rolin', 'Ariel Borysiuk', 'Arouna Kone')
  );

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT T1.player_api_id) FROM Player AS T1 INNER JOIN Player_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.player_api_id = T2.player_api_id WHERE T1.height > 180 AND T2.volleys > 70

selected_schemas.chain_of_thought_reasoning: To answer this question, I need to: 1) Identify the team 'Ajax', 2) Find the maximum chance creation passing score for Ajax, and 3) Find the corresponding chance creation passing class. The team_long_name column is needed to filter for Ajax. The chanceCreationPassing column is needed to find the maximum score. The chanceCreationPassingClass column is needed to retrieve the classification associated with the maximum score. The team_api_id is needed to join the tables.

The question asks for Ajax's highest 'chanceCreationPassing' score and its classification ('chanceCreationPassingClass'). To achieve this, I need to: 1. Join the 'Team' table with the 'Team_Attributes' table to link team names with their attributes. 2. Filter the results to only include the team named 'Ajax' using `Team.team_long_name`. 3. Find the maximum value of `chanceCreationPassing` from the filtered results. 4. Retrieve the corresponding `chanceCreationPassingClass` for that maximum score. Therefore, I need `Team.team_long_name` for filtering, `Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassing` for the score and aggregation, and `Team_Attributes.chanceCreationPassingClass` for the classification. The `Team.id` and `Team_Attributes.team_api_id` (or `team_fifa_api_id`) are necessary for joining the tables.

sql_exec_info.sql: SELECT T2.chanceCreationPassing, T2.chanceCreationPassingClass FROM Team AS T1 INNER JOIN Team_Attributes AS T2 ON T1.team_api_id = T2.team_api_id WHERE T1.team_long_name = 'Ajax' ORDER BY T2.chanceCreationPassing DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 1

CREATE TABLE Country (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for countries,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: country name,
    PRIMARY KEY (id)

);

CREATE TABLE League (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for leagues,
    country_id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for countries,
    name TEXT -- Column Description: league name,
    PRIMARY KEY (id),
    CONSTRAINT fk_League_country_id FOREIGN KEY (country_id) REFERENCES country (id)

);

CREATE TABLE Match (

    id INTEGER -- Column Description: the unique id for matches,
    country_id INTEGER -- Column Description: country id,
    league_id INTEGER -- Column Description: league id,
    season TEXT -- Column Description: the season of the match,
    stage INTEGER -- Column Description: the stage of the match,
    date TEXT -- Column Description: the date of the match, Column Value Explanation: e.g. 2008-08-17 00:00:00,

[

(potential:INTEGER, Description: potential of the player Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  The potential score is between 0-100 which is calculated by FIFA.  Higher potential score means that the player has more potential, Examples: [71, 66, 65, 76, 75]),
(preferred_foot:TEXT, Description: the player's preferred foot when attacking Value Explanation: right/ left, Examples: [right, left]),
(attacking_work_rate:TEXT, Description: the player's attacking work rate Value Explanation: commonsense reasoning:  • high: implies that the player is going to be in all of your attack moves • medium: implies that the player will select the attack actions he will join in • low: remain in his position while the team attacks, Examples: [medium, high, low, None]),
